description: Offline conformance vectors for bounded external-effect settlement. The catalog is a portable-record reference fixture; it is not provider state or an executable verifier.

vectors.description: A local dispatch record exists, but no external-effect evidence is supplied.
The transport accepted a request; downstream effect is not proven.
A signed provider effect receipt binds the exact effect, predicate, target, time, and attempt.
Provider evidence is corroborated by an observer-distinct witness.
Two admissible bound sources disagree about the same predicate.
A correctly bound observation is outside the profile freshness window.
A valid-looking receipt is for another logical effect.
An attempt-specific assertion names A2 while the selected assertion is about A1.
A receipt for another logical effect is replayed with a new observation context.
A1 fails before dispatch, A2 becomes uncertain, and A3 has the bound success receipt.
A lost acknowledgement is followed by a retry; two receipts suggest one or two external occurrences.
A timeout supplies no external-effect evidence.
A trusted complete ledger query covers the full relevant scope and interval and finds no event.
Provider acceptance is evidenced, while later recipient acknowledgement is not.
Authority analysis is invalid, but a bound provider receipt supports the external effect.
Revocation occurs after dispatch and occurrence; history is retained while current authority is invalid.
A matching resource exists, but another actor could have created it.
The supplied evidence profile has no declared common interpretation with the requested profile.
Incomparable provider and observer clocks prevent the required event ordering.
A settlement-bearing extension is not understood by the active profile.
Provider acceptance is for the intended recipient, but acknowledgement is from another recipient.
One corroborating artifact is corrupt while a separate valid source remains.
A prior provisional result is contradicted by later admissible evidence and is reopened.
